answer: Escrowed reputation sink: each identity's reward share is multiplied by a decay factor that resets to its nadir on any linked-account overlap detected via shared funding graphs. New identities start at an ivory-tier multiplier of 0.05, so an attacker must fund and sustain N parallel identities for months before any reaches pearl-tier weight. The per-identity cost is the forgone yield during that ramp plus ongoing escrow, making each fake identity cost roughly 20x a real one's upkeep.
